paper_style.palette_strategy: Local semantic palettes: categorical curves in Figures 1, 2, and 5; a blue dark/light aggregate-versus-raw hierarchy in Figures 4 and 7; panel-specific curves plus a light phase fill in Figure 3; teal text highlighting in Tables 1 and 4. No single global subgrammar/pretraining token is reused across all objects.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Charts are embedded PNG/raster objects inside a vector/text PDF; captions, body text, formulas, and tables are PDF text/vector objects. Figure 6a is visibly lower resolution than Figure 6b and the other chart rasters.
paper_style.style_consistency: Roman body/caption typography, italic object labels, small multiples, and booktabs-like tables are consistent enough for a workshop paper. Chart font sizing, palette tokens, and raster resolution vary; Table 2 is larger than the result tables.

figures.label: Figure 1a–b
figures.module: §4.2 Experiments and Visualizations; inner-subgrammar KL decomposition and parallel learning

caption.text: Figure 1. Experiments visualizing decomposition of KL-divergence (Theorems 4.3 and 4.5) over subgrammars, and parallel learning of subgrammars “overhead" refers to constant strings in between subgrammar roots. Full grammars defined in Appendix D.

color.semantic_mapping: L1 is orange; subgrammar L2, L2_2, and L2_3 are magenta, green, and blue; overhead is cyan. Legends and matching circular trajectories carry the identity mapping.

encodings.facet: Panel a: inner subgrammars at 100% probability; panel b: L2/L2_2/L2_3 with probabilities 0.3/0.3/0.4
encodings.text: Per-panel legends and colored brace/value decomposition annotations

figures.data_and_statistics: Deterministic training trajectories; no error bars, bands, seed dispersion, or hypothesis test. Panel b states that every D_KL term is weighted by probability p and that the displayed terms should sum. The linked analysis_hierarchy.py supports Epochs/KL-divergence plotting and 300 dpi export, but its checked-in random-color/no-marker defaults do not exactly reproduce this PDF.
figures.evidence_relation: Direct visual evidence for Theorems 4.3, 4.5, and 4.6: component losses decompose over subgrammars and learning proceeds in parallel. Appendix D defines the grammars and Appendix C supplies proof details.
design_strengths: Matched panels make the probability-weighted decomposition inspectable.
A common x/y grammar and explicit legend make component trajectories comparable.
Colored brace annotations connect plotted terms to the theorem arithmetic.
design_weaknesses: Five hue-dependent categories are weak in grayscale.
The caption does not define the exact plotted quantity, seed/model setup, or brace computation.
The public helper source differs from the rendered marker/color styling, limiting exact reproduction.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair deterministic and probability-weighted structural cases in matched small multiples, preserve identical axes, and add a compact arithmetic annotation that readers can verify.

figures.label: Figure 2a–b
figures.module: §4.2 Experiments and Visualizations; deeper-recursion and outer-subgrammar examples

caption.text: Figure 2. Additional examples of how loss, or KL-divergence, behaves with respect to varying subgrammar structure.

color.semantic_mapping: Panel a maps L0–L4 to blue, orange, magenta, brown, and gray; panel b maps L0 and outer subgrammar to indigo and pink. Circular markers duplicate the trajectory identity.

encodings.facet: Panel a: depth-4 inner-subgrammar DAG; panel b: outer-subgrammar decomposition

figures.data_and_statistics: Single training trajectories with no seed-level dispersion or uncertainty. analysis_hierarchy.py supports the Epochs/KL trajectory idiom, and def_pcfgs.py contains the deeper-recursion and outer-subgrammar grammar definitions; no exact PDF asset or table of plotted values is public.
figures.evidence_relation: Extends Figure 1's theorem visualization to a depth-4 inner recursion and the outer-subgrammar case covered by Theorem C.2, supporting the decomposition across varied structures.
design_strengths: Matched panels let the reader transfer the Figure 1 visual grammar.
Depth is made visible through labels and ordered colors.
The two-curve outer-subgrammar panel is especially legible.
design_weaknesses: Panel-specific legends and palettes impede cross-panel category comparison.
The caption does not define L0–L4 or identify the model/training conditions.
No uncertainty is shown for what is described as qualitative behavior.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep a fixed small-multiple template while varying structural complexity, and add shared semantic colors or direct labels when depth categories must be compared across panels.

figures.label: Figure 3a–c

caption.text: Figure 3. Examples of pretraining on differently placed subgrammars using ABC Grammar.

color.semantic_mapping: L0 is dark blue in every panel; the location-specific subgrammar is purple for prefix, magenta for infix, and dark red for suffix; a light-gray fill marks pretraining.

encodings.facet: Prefix, infix, and suffix subgrammar placement
encodings.text: Per-panel legend and pretrain-on-subgrammar phase label

figures.data_and_statistics: One trajectory per displayed condition; no seed dispersion, error band, or interval. analysis_hierarchy.py supports trajectory plotting and def_pcfgs.py defines ABC Grammar, but the checked-in plotting function does not exactly reproduce the PDF marker/color choices.
figures.evidence_relation: §5.1 location-sensitivity evidence: pretraining preserves subgrammar modeling when the subgrammar is a prefix, infix, or suffix. This is a location factor experiment, not a component-deletion ablation.
design_strengths: Identical axes make the location comparison immediate.
The shaded phase boundary separates pretraining from full-grammar training.
Trajectories expose transfer dynamics rather than only endpoint values.
design_weaknesses: Per-panel colors prevent one fixed subgrammar identity from being tracked across locations.
No uncertainty is shown despite the narrative using reliable retention language.
Repeating legends and phase keys consumes plotting area.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use aligned small multiples with a common phase band for training-stage comparisons; keep the baseline hue stable and reserve a secondary encoding for the manipulated location.

figures.label: Figure 4a–b

caption.text: Figure 4. LM error vs. longer context, with or without recursion

color.semantic_mapping: Dark blue is the average; pale blue is individual raw runs; pure blue is the endpoint/plateau annotation. Lightness and line weight duplicate the aggregate/raw distinction.

encodings.line: Solid trajectories plus dashed plateau guide
encodings.facet: Nonrecursive depth-0 contexts versus recursive depth-i contexts
encodings.text: Average legend, endpoint values 0.017/0.173, and plateau guide values

figures.data_and_statistics: Multiple raw seed/run trajectories are shown behind an average; no confidence band or formal uncertainty summary is encoded. depth_recursion_exp.py specifies pale raw lines in #80A0DB at alpha 0.5, a #002FD8 average at linewidth 2.5, blue dashed plateau guides and bold values, Sequence Depth/Prediction Error axes, upper-left legend, and a 0–0.25 y-limit.
figures.evidence_relation: Direct §6 evidence for the failure boundary: nonrecursive/shallow contexts stay at low error, while deeper recursive contexts accumulate error with depth. Figure 7 tests prefix sensitivity of this depth response.
design_strengths: Raw runs plus an aggregate preserve heterogeneity.
Matched axes and direct endpoint labels make the contrast legible.
Light/dark and line-weight encoding is more robust than a many-hue palette.
design_weaknesses: Pale runs are not explicitly identified as seeds or uncertainty in the legend/caption.
Endpoint labels and guide lines are not fully defined.
The panel-b formula has a malformed/missing parenthesis in the PDF.
A single average can conceal divergence among raw runs.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show raw trajectories behind a heavier aggregate and annotate only the endpoint/plateau needed for the claim; define raw-run semantics in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5. Two-layer Transformer showing the impact of the probability of recursion.

color.semantic_mapping: Recursion probabilities p=0.60, 0.70, 0.80, and 0.90 map to blue, orange, green, and red curves.

encodings.text: Legend p values and axis labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Deterministic curves for four p settings; no seed or uncertainty display. src/kl.py specifies the four curves, Mini-batch Iterations/KL Divergence labels, 4 × 3 inch figure, legend, and 300 dpi export. Appendix E.2 gives the two-rule CFG and connects the p sensitivity to expected recursion.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix visual support for Theorem 4.6: changing the probability of nonrecursive expansion changes recursive KL behavior in the predicted direction.
design_strengths: Four curves make the one-factor monotonic effect immediate.
A compact legend and single axis keep the theoretical mechanism focused.
design_weaknesses: Color is the sole condition encoding.
No repeated-run or uncertainty information is shown.
The caption omits the exact p values and grammar equation that appear in the preceding prose.
figures.reusable_pattern: For a one-factor theory sensitivity, use one shared axis and put the factor values in a direct legend; repeat essential factor levels in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 6a–b

caption.text: Figure 6. Distribution of final KL value of pretraining versus training from scratch

color.semantic_mapping: Black encodes box/whisker outlines and orange encodes the median. Position and box geometry provide redundant condition/distribution encodings.

encodings.x: Training condition: from scratch versus with pretraining
encodings.color: Orange median versus black distribution outline

design_strengths: Boxplots expose spread and outliers rather than only a mean.
Black/orange median treatment remains legible without a legend.
Panel labels directly identify model depth.
design_weaknesses: The panels use different y ranges, complicating cross-panel comparison.
The caption omits n and whisker semantics.
Panel a is visibly lower-resolution than panel b.
The prose claim and panel-b median appear inconsistent.

figures.label: Figure 7a–c
figures.module: Appendix E.4 Generalization and Prefix Experiments

caption.text: Figure 7. Comparison of different prefixes for recursion type 2

color.semantic_mapping: Dark blue is the average, pale blue is the raw-run source color #80A0DB rendered at alpha 0.5 (visible as approximately #BFCFEC on white), and pure blue is the endpoint/guide annotation.

encodings.color: Average versus individual raw runs versus guide annotation
encodings.facet: Valid terminal prefix, valid nested-bracket prefix, and invalid prefix
encodings.text: Average legend, prefix strings, and endpoint values 0.166/0.166/0.163

figures.data_and_statistics: Same depth-completion evaluation as Figure 4 with three prefix conditions. Individual runs and an average are plotted, with no interval or formal uncertainty. depth_recursion_exp.py provides the raw/average construction, direct final-value labels, guide annotations, and 0–0.25 y scale. Appendix text reports endpoints around 0.16–0.17 at depth 200 and interprets the near-equality as prefix-insensitivity.
figures.evidence_relation: Direct Appendix E.4 evidence that error is governed primarily by recursive depth rather than prefix context or grammatical validity; this probes a failure mechanism rather than training-time optimization.
design_strengths: Matched panels make the invariance claim inspectable.
An intentionally invalid prefix is a useful stress control.
Raw runs prevent near-equality from being only a mean-level claim.
design_weaknesses: The caption omits the near-equal endpoint finding and raw-run semantics.
Dense parenthesis strings are difficult to parse at small size.
No direct numerical uncertainty summary accompanies the many runs.
Repeated legends consume space.
figures.reusable_pattern: Compare valid and invalid context controls in aligned panels while holding the continuation task and depth axis fixed; include raw runs when claiming invariance.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Average linear CKA similarity (0–1) across attention and MLP layers of a different, independently trained transformers when pretraining for 10 vs. 20 epochs. After pretraining, the models were trained for additional 45 epochs. The average was computed over off-diagonal seed pairs (30 seeds; 435 pairs) on the evaluation set. The most significant differences are in teal. This experiment was run using PythonPCFG.

tables.uncertainty: No dispersion, interval, or hypothesis-test output is printed. The caption reports 30 seeds and 435 off-diagonal pairs.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three-decimal average linear CKA values are reported for Full grammar sequences, Subgrammar sequences, and Subgrammar pretraining only across Two-layer/ Four-layer, pretraining-10/20-epoch, and Attention/MLP headers. Full-grammar scratch = [0.258, 0.535, 0.249, 0.535, 0.249, 0.469], pretraining = [0.281, 0.534, 0.303, 0.511, 0.323, 0.491], change (%) = [+8.9, -0.2, +21.7, -4.7, +8.3, +1.0]. Subgrammar scratch = [0.298, 0.561, 0.288, 0.558, 0.295, 0.513], pretraining = [0.339, 0.566, 0.348, 0.544, 0.347, 0.525], change (%) = [+13.8, -0.1, +20.8, -2.6, +10.7, +1.9]. tables.evidence_relation: Central §5.2 mechanism evidence for cross-seed activation alignment under subgrammar pretraining on both full-grammar and subgrammar sequences. Appendix B defines linear CKA; Table 4 is a smaller ABC Grammar companion.
design_strengths: Nested headers expose model size and pretraining duration without a separate legend.
The metric range and seed-pair denominator appear in the caption.
Teal highlights direct attention to selected changes.
design_weaknesses: Most significant has no operational threshold or test definition.
Printed percentage changes are not consistently reproducible by the ordinary relative formula; for example 0.249 to 0.323 is about +29.7% while the table prints +8.3%.
The spanning table requires small type and color.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use multi-level headers and explicit aggregation denominators for representation comparisons, and define highlighting and percentage formulas in the caption or a note.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: The main text moves from theorem decomposition (Figures 1–2), to representation alignment (Table 1), to location robustness (Figure 3), and finally to the recursive-depth failure boundary (Figure 4). The appendix adds configuration lookup (Table 2), recursion-probability mechanism (Figure 5), seed-level distributions (Figure 6), cosine mechanism slices (Table 3), duration sensitivity (Table 4), and prefix controls (Figure 7).
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure captions use an italic Figure label, short descriptive title, and setup sentence; table captions are longer and carry metric definitions, durations, datasets, or denominators. Most captions name what is plotted rather than the main finding. Raw-run semantics, boxplot conventions, and highlighting formulas are under-specified.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1 and 4 share model → pretraining duration → Attention/MLP headers; Table 3 uses semantic sequence row groups and module columns; Table 2 is a flat configuration header. The shared structure is coherent, but percentage-change rows need a common formula note.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: The visual set covers theory, representation/mechanism, location and recursion-probability sensitivity, model-depth and pretraining-duration sensitivity, and prefix controls. There is no component-deletion ablation; ablation here means changing experimental factors such as duration, depth, location, or prefix.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The main text explicitly points to Appendix B for CKA, Appendix C for proofs, Appendix D for grammar definitions, and Appendix E for Figures 5–7 and Tables 3–4. The appendix extends rather than replaces the main narrative.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Roman body/caption text and italic labels are stable. Embedded chart labels are smaller sans text, Table 2 is larger than result tables, and Figure 6a's lower raster resolution is a notable outlier.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/pale-blue aggregate/raw encoding recurs in Figures 4 and 7; categorical palettes reset across Figures 1–3 and 5; teal has a stable table-highlighting role in Tables 1 and 4. There is no project-wide semantic color token for subgrammar identity or pretraining.

most_reusable_patterns: Theorem-facing paired small multiples with inspectable decompositions.
Matched location/depth/prefix panels with a common axis grammar.
Raw trajectories behind a heavier aggregate.
Multi-level result headers with explicit seed-pair denominators.
highest_value_objects: Figure 6: distributional complement to average-level comparisons.
failure_patterns: Captions generally omit the main finding and raw-run/whisker semantics.
Hue is overused without consistent shape or line redundancy.
Figure 6 panels use different y ranges and panel a has lower raster resolution.
Tables 1 and 4 leave percentage-change and most-significant definitions unresolved.
The public source repository contains only partial matches to the rendered PDF.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses theorem-linked, color-coded small multiples to move from additive subgrammar loss to representation and recursion-depth evidence, with appendix tables and raw-run/distribution views supplying factor sensitivity while leaving several statistical and rendering conventions implicit.
